item.research_question: How does the microstructure and mechanical behavior of the Al0.35CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy change when processed via additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) compared to its cast and heat-treated state, particularly regarding strain-rate sensitivity?
item.material_system: Al0.35CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (nominal composition, cast from 99% purity elements)
item.processing_route: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) using a B8 machine; 15-layer build with 1 mm layer height, 500 rpm spindle rotation, 31.8 mm/min traversing speed, and 27.9 mm/min actuator feed rate; feedstock annealed at 750 °C for 24 h and water-quenched.
item.test_conditions: Compression testing at quasi-static (0.001 s⁻¹) and intermediate (1 s⁻¹) strain rates in ambient laboratory conditions; specimen dimensions: 4.5 mm height and 4.5 mm diameter.
key_findings: The AFSD process reduced grain size significantly, with EBSD revealing reduced grain sizes along bands of aluminum-rich particles at layer interfaces.
The maximum stress of the AFSD material was 1074 MPa at 0.001 s⁻¹, approximately double the feedstock's 576 MPa.
The advancing side (AS) of the deposit contained a fully FCC structure, while the retreating side (RS) exhibited a dual-phase FCC/BCC structure.
Al-rich particles were observed along layer interfaces on the retreating side, with EDS confirming their composition.
The average annealed hardness of the feedstock was ~175 HV, while the AFSD material showed significantly increased hardness at Al-rich locations.
The feedstock material showed positive strain-rate sensitivity, with maximum stress increasing from 575 MPa (0.001 s⁻¹) to 690 MPa (1 s⁻¹).
The AFSD material exhibited apparent strain-rate insensitivity, with maximum stresses of 1074 MPa (0.001 s⁻¹) and 1057 MPa (1 s⁻¹).

The feedstock material showed pronounced softening indicative of resistance to dynamic recrystallization (DRX), whereas the AFSD material showed stage-III and stage-IV hardening characteristic of DRX.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strength increase to the Hall–Petch effect from grain refinement and the formation of a split FCC + BCC phase structure. Grain refinement in the AFSD material is attributed to dynamic recrystallization (DRX) and Zener pinning by Al-rich particles at layer interfaces. The resistance to recrystallization in the cast feedstock is attributed to sluggish diffusion behavior.
item.limitations: The authors note that the apparent strain-rate insensitivity in the AFSD material may be due to the placement of samples taken from both the advancing and retreating sides of the deposit, which have different local mechanical properties and hardness levels.
item.future_work: The authors propose that further mechanical performance could be gained from the implementation of a post-deposition heat treatment to dissolve the Al-rich particles and further increase the BCC structure.
quotes: The overall strength of the deposited material was approximately doubled compared to that of the cast material system with increases in strength at both quasi-static and intermediate strain rates due to the Hall–Petch effect and a split FCC + BCC phase structure.
The reduced grain sizes in these bands suggest Zener pinning, from the Al-rich particles, was impeding the grain growth of the dynamically recrystallized grains.
Sluggish diffusion behavior is reported as the culprit for AlCoCrFeNi alloy systems' resistance to recrystallization.
